newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain condemns Rwanda killing, offers repatriation.
newsitem.headline: Spain condemns Rwanda killing, offers repatriation.

text.p: Spain condemned on Sunday the murder of three Spanish aid workers in Rwanda and advised its citizens in the region to leave as soon as possible.

"We condemn the killings and have sent condolences to the families and now we are concentrating on getting the corpses back and advising those still there to leave," Foreign Ministry spokesman Inocencio Arias said.
Rwandan Hutu militiamen shot dead three Spanish aid workers and three soldiers and seriously wounded an American in an overnight attack in the northwestern town of Ruhengeri.
Arias said Spain's ambassador in Tanzania had left for Rwanda under orders to repatriate the bodies of the three Spaniards and to offer repatriation to those remaining in the area.
"Our ambassador will tell those left in the Great Lakes region that we advise them to leave...we will tell them to go to Kigali from where we will take them out of the country," Arias said.
The Spaniards, who had been shot through the head, were attached to Medicos del Mundo (Doctors of the World), a Spanish aid organisation.
The organisation said on Sunday it had suspended its activities in Rwanda until the situation could be reassessed.

"We are sending four or five people to Rwanda who will take care of the corpses and will reassess the situation to see whether we go on with our project or suspend our activities permanently," a spokesman for Medicos del Mundo in Madrid said.
"We don't actually know what exactly happened, we only know they were killed but we have different versions of how," he added.

An American diplomat in Rwanda said the attackers had stormed into the house and demanded the Spaniards' passports, but were then disturbed by the noise of gunfire outside the house, and reacted by shooting the three at close range.
Arias said around 110 Spaniards, many of them church volunteers, remained in Rwanda.
